course.title: Bead Making and Jewellery
course.tagline: Make beaded necklaces, bracelets and waist beads people love to wear.

days.title: Jewellery Making Basics
days.goal: Know the tools and materials of bead jewellery.

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Learn the tools: pliers, cutters, beading needle and thread.
Learn the materials: beads, cord, clasps and findings (the small metal parts).
Learn bead sizes: small beads are 4mm, big beads are 10mm.
Set up a bead mat so beads do not roll away.
days.task: Label your tools and materials.
days.challenge: Name three tools and what each does.

quiz.q: What are findings in jewellery making?
options: The small metal parts like clasps and rings
quiz.explain: Findings are the small metal parts: clasps, jump rings and hooks.

quiz.q: Why use a bead mat?
options: So beads do not roll away
quiz.explain: A bead mat has a soft surface that stops beads rolling off the table.

quiz.q: What size is a small bead?
quiz.explain: Small beads are about 4mm across; big beads are about 10mm.

days.title: Bead Types: Glass, Wood, Stone and Plastic

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Hold glass, wood, stone and plastic beads.

Learn that wood beads are light and suit casual bracelets.

days.task: Sort beads into glass, wood, stone and plastic.
days.challenge: Pick the best bead type for a bracelet and explain why.

quiz.q: What are findings in jewellery making?
options: The small metal parts like clasps and rings
quiz.explain: Findings are the small metal parts: clasps, jump rings and hooks.

quiz.q: Why use a bead mat?
options: So beads do not roll away
quiz.explain: A bead mat has a soft surface that stops beads rolling off the table.

quiz.q: What size is a small bead?

days.title: Stringing Beads

video.title: 5 Essential Jewelry Making Techniques

steps: Cut cord a little longer than you need.
Thread beads in your pattern, checking the colours.
Keep the beads snug with no gaps.
Tie a strong knot and hide it inside a bead.
days.task: String a bracelet with a neat pattern.
days.challenge: String beads with no gaps and no loose cord.

days.title: Bracelet Sizes and Fit
days.goal: Measure wrists and make bracelets that fit.

video.title: How to Make Beaded Bracelets and Pearl Necklaces

steps: Measure a wrist with a tape around the bone.
Add about 1cm for comfort.
Learn that a tight bracelet is uncomfortable and breaks easily.
Test the fit on a real wrist before you finish.
days.task: Measure three wrists and record the sizes.
days.challenge: Make a bracelet that fits a wrist well.

quiz.q: Which beads suit a casual bracelet?
quiz.explain: Wood beads are light and suit casual everyday bracelets.

quiz.q: Why are stone beads heavy?
quiz.explain: Stone is dense, so stone beads feel heavy compared with wood or plastic.

quiz.q: Which beads shine the most?
quiz.explain: Glass beads catch light and shine, so they suit necklaces.
